sentences.text: Revenue moved from $41.9 billion in FY2016 to $47.9 billion in FY2025, a 1.5% CAGR [F1][F10][F219].
The path was a step down then a rebuild: revenue fell 13.5% in FY2017 and 5.3% in FY2018 before recovering to $45.8 billion by FY2023 [D42][D93][F8].
The FY2017 decline came with refranchising of bottling operations, which cut operating cash flow that year [P75].
Operating income compounded at 5.3% against revenue's 1.5%, and net income at 8.1%, so profit outgrew the top line over the window [F221][F219][F222].
FY2025 was the sharpest inflection, with operating income up 37.7% on lower other operating charges after the prior-year fairlife contingent consideration remeasurement [D450][P12].
Concentrate operations supplied 59.4% of FY2025 revenue and 1.6pp of its 1.9% growth, while finished product operations added 0.3pp [D532][D534][D449][D541].
Within concentrate, the non-US piece contributed 1.3pp of FY2025 growth on 3.1% growth, and US concentrate added 0.3pp [D548][D547][D569].
Non-US finished product operations shrank 4.9% and subtracted 1.0pp, offsetting part of the concentrate gain [D554][D555].
Worldwide concentrate sales volume grew 1% in FY2025, with EMEA up 4% and pricing favorable, per the filing [P12][P10].
Operating income grew 37.7% against 1.9% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 428.4%, so operating leverage was extreme but driven by the charge comparison [D450][D449][D473].
Operating margin reached 28.7% in FY2025, a window high against a 26.0% median and 20.7% low [F50][D765][D766][D764].
Gross margin was 61.6%, up 0.6pp, within a window that ran from 58.1% to 62.1% [F30][D462][D770][D771].
The FY2025 operating margin rose 7.5pp, with 6.2pp from other lines, 0.7pp from SG&A and 0.6pp from cost of revenue [D463][D477][D476][D475].
The other-line swing reflects lower other operating charges after the prior-year fairlife remeasurement, while SG&A fell on lower Foundation contributions and incentive expense [P12][P13].
Net margin of 27.3% exceeded operating margin's move because other income of $1,073 million and a 17.9% tax rate lifted below-the-line results [F70][X100][D435].
Operating cash flow of $7.4 billion and free cash flow of $5.3 billion were 15.5% and 11.0% of revenue in FY2025 [F100][F120][D434][D433].
Free cash flow covered only 0.40x of net income, the window low against a 0.97x median, and ranked 0th percentile versus staples peers [D437][D776][D778][D795].
FY2024's collapse to $6.8 billion operating cash flow came from a $6.0 billion IRS tax litigation deposit and refranchising effects [F99][P22].
Capex of $2.1 billion was 4.4% of revenue and 2.01x D&A, the highest multiple in the window [F110][D432][D438].
Net cash was $8.8 billion, or 18.3% of revenue, in FY2025 against a staples peer median of -14.5%, ranking 100th percentile [D442][D443][D794][D793].
Total debt of $1.5 billion in FY2025 rose 31.3% from $1.1 billion, though both are far below the $41.7 billion of FY2023 [D441][D391][D340].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.5 billion were 179.9% of free cash flow, the third straight year above 100% [D444][D445].
Diluted shares fell only 0.2% in FY2025, so per-share growth tracked net income growth rather than buyback accretion [D468][D453][D451].

Revenue for FY2017 and FY2018 in the table is a later recast, $36.2 billion and $34.3 billion versus $35.4 billion and $31.9 billion first reported, so growth spanning those years mixes presentations [R1][F2][X2][F3][X3].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2024 and FY2025, at 0.45x and 0.40x, a two-year deterioration [R3][D387][D437].
Payout exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, reaching 214.2% in FY2024, which is only sustainable while the balance sheet absorbs it [R2][D344][D395][D445].
Total debt rose 31% in FY2025, a one-period move off a very low base [R4][D441][D391].
Free cash flow over net income: a recovery toward the 0.97x window median would confirm the FY2024 tax deposit was the main drag, while staying near the 0.40x low would not [D778][D776].
Operating margin: holding above the 26.0% window median would confirm the FY2025 charge-driven gain is durable, while a fall back toward the 21.2% of FY2024 would reverse it [D766][F49].
Buybacks plus dividends against free cash flow: a move back below the 105.1% of FY2023 would show capital return resizing to cash generation [D344].
